QUIC stream spam test with handshake, payload checks, and connection cleanup.

# Purpose
This file is a QUIC integration test executable. It creates a server `fd_quic_t` instance and a client `fd_quic_t` instance in the same workspace, connects them with `fd_quic_virtual_pair_init`, and drives both sides with repeated calls to `fd_quic_service`. The test checks two main behaviors: the handshake completes on both sides, and stream data received by the server matches the payload generated by `fd_quic_stream_spam_gen` for each stream ID and offset. The [`my_stream_rx_cb`](<#my_stream_rx_cb>) callback validates stream length and content, then counts received streams until the test reaches 10,000 received stream events.

The file also checks configuration and lifecycle behavior for the QUIC implementation. The [`test_invalid_tx_buf_sz`](<#test_invalid_tx_buf_sz>) function verifies that `fd_quic_new` rejects an invalid transmit buffer size. In [`main`](<#main>), the code creates a workspace, sets server and client limits, installs callbacks such as [`my_connection_new`](<#my_connection_new>), [`my_handshake_complete`](<#my_handshake_complete>), and `fd_quic_stream_spam_notify`, starts a connection with `fd_quic_connect`, sends stream traffic with `fd_quic_stream_spam_service`, then closes the connection and waits for ACK processing before cleaning up all objects.
